$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-2={X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-4=-2{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(s-1){X}_{1}(s)-3{X}_{2}(s)=2 \\ 2{X}_{1}(s)+(s-1){X}_{2}(s)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{4-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-1)[\frac{4-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)}{2}]-3{X}_{2}(s) & =2 \\ 4(s-1)-(s-1)^{2}{X}_{2}(s)-6{X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ 4(s-1)-[(s-1)^{2}+6]{X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ 4(s-1)-({s}^{2}-2s+7){X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ -({s}^{2}-2s+7){X}_{2}(s) & =4-4(s-1) \\ -({s}^{2}-2s+7){X}_{2}(s) & =-4s+8 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{4(s-2)}{{s}^{2}-2s+7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{4-(s-1){X}_{2}(s)}{2} \\  & =\frac{4-(s-1)\cdot \frac{4(s-2)}{{s}^{2}-2s+7}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4({s}^{2}-2s+7)-(s-1)\cdot 4(s-2)}{2({s}^{2}-2s+7)} \\  & =\frac{4{s}^{2}-8s+28-4(s-1)(s-2)}{2({s}^{2}-2s+7)} \\  & =\frac{4s+20}{2({s}^{2}-2s+7)} \\  & =\frac{2(s+5)}{{s}^{2}-2s+7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2(s+5)}{{s}^{2}-2s+7},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{4(s-2)}{{s}^{2}-2s+7}.
$$

First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-2{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-4=2{X}_{1}(s)-3{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+2=-2{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(s-2){X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)=4 \\ 2{X}_{1}(s)+(s-3){X}_{2}(s)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-2)[\frac{-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)}{2}]+3{X}_{2}(s) & =4 \\ (s-2)[-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)]+6{X}_{2}(s) & =8 \\ -2(s-2)-[(s-2)(s-3)-6]{X}_{2}(s) & =8 \\ -({s}^{2}-5s){X}_{2}(s) & =8+2(s-2) \\ -s(s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =2s+4 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-2(s+2)}{s(s-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-2-(s-3){X}_{2}(s)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2-(s-3)\cdot \frac{-2(s+2)}{s(s-5)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2s(s+5)+2(s-3)(s+2)}{2s(s-5)} \\  & =\frac{2(2s-3)}{s(s-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2(2s-3)}{s(s-5)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-2(s+2)}{s(s-5)}.
$$

By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{2}{s-3},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{1}{s-3}-\frac{3}{s-1}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

questions.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{2}{s-3}\} \\  & =2{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\  & =2{e}^{3\cdot t} \\  & =2{e}^{3t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}-\frac{3}{s-1}\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\}-3{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-1}\} \\  & ={e}^{3\cdot t}-3{e}^{1\cdot t} \\  & ={e}^{3t}-3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{3t}-3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$
